newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai IPO mkt seen sluggish on slumping bourse.
newsitem.headline: Thai IPO mkt seen sluggish on slumping bourse.

text.p: The bearish mood on the Thai stock market will significantly affect the initial public offering market due to a lack of investor demand for new shares, investment bankers said.
"It's not good timing to float any new share right now. The stock market is very bearish," Prinyar Prinyarnussorn, vice president at General Finance and Securities Plc, told Reuters.
The unfavourable market condition will reduce investors' demand for any new issues as they can buy cheap stock on the exchange, he said.

Kasom Piriyakich, vice-president at Pacific Finance and Securities said: "I don't see any new fresh incentives to help shore up the battered stock market in the near term. The sluggish economy has affected all industries and reduced fund demand for new investments."
Thai stocks tumbled to more than a four-year low in early January as the bourse was hit by political uncertainty and signs of a sharp slowdown in the economy, brokers said.

The Bank of Thailand had projected 1996 gross domestic product to grow by 6.7 percent - the slowest growth in a decade. The central bank, however, said it saw a moderate recovery for the national economy in 1997, with GDP growth expanding to 7.1 percent.
"We won't see many new share issues in the first half. Most issuers decided to postpone their (IPO) flotation right now," Prinyar said.

According to the Securities and Exchange Commission, the value of funds raised through initial public share offerings in 1996 totalled 87.64 billion baht ($3.37 billion), against 62.04 billion in the previous year.
Analysts say the most interesting issues in 1997 will be the IPOs of Bangkok Transit System Corp (BTSC), a mass transit unit of property developer Tanayong Plc, and Submicron Technology Plc.
BTSC holds the 30-year concession to operate and build a rail system in Bangkok due to open in 1998. The project will cost about $1.68 billion.
Submicron, which aims to be Thailand's first wafer fabrication facility, last December indefinitely delayed its IPO flotation plan citing poor stock market sentiment.
"The entertainment sector will also have some attractive IPOs this year. There are four or five (entertainment) stocks planning to float their IPOs," Prinyar said.
